note_en: 由于 introduces a cause, like English "because of" or "due to," and is more formal than 因为: 由于越来越多的游客想尝正宗的上海小吃，这家店几乎每天都排着长队 "Because more and more tourists want to try authentic Shanghai snacks, there's a long line almost every day." Chinese puts the cause first and the result second, the reverse of the common English order "there's a line because…"
